transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

Well, I came in because... most days I just wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling right in my chest. It's like the old Ruben—the guy who could talk to anybody and actually enjoy his day—is just gone.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It's been about eight months now. It all started around the time they brought in a new regional manager at work. He started really coming down on me, just... taking away accounts that I’d been handling for years. So, yeah, right around then.
Have you ever experienced a period in the past where you felt down or depressed like this?
No... no, I haven't. I mean, I've had bad days before, sure, like anybody else. But never anything like this. This is the first time I've ever felt... well, just completely stuck like this.
Have you ever had times where you felt the complete opposite—unusually energized, elated, or on top of the world, with much less need for sleep?

No, I... no, I can't say I've ever felt like that. I mean, sure, I've had good days—maybe closed a big account and felt happy about it—but nothing like what you're describing. I've always needed my regular sleep. I've never been, you know, unusually energized or anything. Just... just a regular guy, really, until all this started.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in doing things you used to enjoy?

Yeah, I have. I used to really look forward to things, you know? Like bowling, or getting out and working in the garden. I used to take my wife to gallery shows, or we'd go dancing. But now... I just don't care about any of it. I just sit there and make up excuses not to go, because none of it even feels worth the effort anymore.
How has your sleep been during these past eight months?

It's been pretty bad. At night, I just lie there... I can't seem to shut my brain off. I end up replaying work stuff over and over, just staring up at the ceiling. And then, even when I finally manage to drift off, I'm wide awake again by three or four in the morning. I wake up feeling completely worn out already, just... dreading having to get through another day.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite during this time?
No, not really. My appetite's been about the same as it always is. I mean, I still eat my regular meals. I haven't noticed any big changes there.
How have your energy levels been throughout the day?

I'm not really sure. I mean, like I said, I wake up feeling pretty worn out from not sleeping well. But as for the rest of the day... I haven't really noticed any big changes. I guess my energy is just about normal once I actually get going. I haven't really paid much attention to it, to be honest.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating, focusing on tasks, or making everyday decisions?

No, I haven't really had any trouble with that. My focus is... well, it's fine. I can still pay attention to what I need to do for work, talk to my clients, that sort of thing. And making decisions hasn't been an issue either. I just haven't noticed any problems there.
Have you been struggling with feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt about things?

Yeah, I have. I just... I keep telling myself I'm useless now. It feels like all those years of taking care of my clients and providing for my family, like none of it even counts anymore. I just feel like a failure because I can't even handle this job right now. It's just... it's heavy, you know?
During this difficult time, have you had any thoughts of harming yourself, or feeling like you would be better off dead?

Yeah... I have. I've been having these thoughts lately that... maybe my wife and kids would just be better off if I didn't wake up in the morning. It's hard to admit that, but it's true. And, honestly, those thoughts scare me. I just... I don't really trust myself the way I used to right now.
